evidence_candidates.claim: Increasing diesel energy share strengthens and spreads the pilot flame, accelerating the initial H2 reaction, while the late mixing-controlled phase remains similar across energy shares.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Pressure/aHRR and flame images show a larger pilot and faster early H2 flame development as H2 share decreases from 95% to 70%.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Natural-luminosity thresholds and two imaging arrangements limit quantitative cross-sweep intensity comparison.

evidence_candidates.claim: Advancing H2 injection changes the premixed/mixing-controlled balance and the 30 CA bTDC case significantly delays diesel pilot ignition, attributed to preignition dilution.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: aHRR and flame images separate timing-dependent interaction, premixing and delayed pilot ignition.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Fuel distributions before ignition were not directly visualized; dilution is author interpretation.
